description: FR-OFF-015 identifier discipline, and GD-D1-01 (ratified 2026-09-02): the permanent 128-bit client identifier is a ULID, rendered on the ROS wire/API as the repository-standard canonical UUID hexadecimal string. Only the decisions actually implemented in the protocol kernel are graded here.

rendering.description: The same 128 bits in both encodings, derived from the Crockford alphabet 0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ: the first 10 characters are the 48-bit millisecond timestamp (here 1727641790304), the remaining 16 are the 80-bit random component (here 10). A client that generates a ULID must send the UUID rendering; base32 is not the ROS API representation.

acceptedWireForm.description: The repository's UUID_PATTERN is case-insensitive; PostgreSQL normalises to lowercase on storage.

A ULID-derived id is a valid uuid VALUE but is NOT RFC-4122 — its version/variant nibbles are data, not a version tag. An RFC-strict validator would wrongly reject every client-generated id, which is why src/common/ids.ts ships a deliberately lenient UUID_PATTERN.
GD-D1-01: base32 is an alternate representation of the same ULID, not the canonical ROS API representation. Accepting both would put two encodings of one identifier into one API.

serverNeverRemaps.description: FR-OFF-015: 'The server SHALL NOT reassign identifiers.' At the protocol level this is observable: whatever opId and entityId the client sent are the values the server stores and echoes back, byte for byte, in every result — accepted, duplicate, conflict, rejected and deferred alike.
